_doc: Shared Mermaid config for the rulebook flowcharts. The web page loads the dark values from reference.njk; scripts/build-pdf.py passes this file to mermaid-cli for the printed book, which is why the palette here is the light one. Geometry and type are the same in both so the charts read as one set.
themeCSS: .node rect, .node polygon, .node circle, .node path { rx: 0 !important; ry: 0 !important; stroke-width: 1.4px !important; } .edgePath .path { stroke-width: 1.2px !important; } .edgeLabel { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace !important; font-size: 10px !important; letter-spacing: 0.08em !important; text-transform: uppercase !important; } .marker { stroke-width: 1.2px !important; } .node .label { font-family: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif !important; } g.node.start rect, g.node.start polygon, g.node.start path { fill: #d8ecf0 !important; stroke: #1a6b7a !important; } g.node.good rect, g.node.good polygon, g.node.good path { fill: #dfe8d5 !important; stroke: #3f5e2a !important; } g.node.bad rect, g.node.bad polygon, g.node.bad path { fill: #f0dcd6 !important; stroke: #8e2f23 !important; } g.node.warn rect, g.node.warn polygon, g.node.warn path { fill: #f2e4c4 !important; stroke: #8a6512 !important; } g.node.spell rect, g.node.spell polygon, g.node.spell path { fill: #e2e9f0 !important; stroke: #2a5a6b !important; }
